name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA. Its MoE design cuts latency 30-40% while keeping quality high, freeing up compute for more tasks. The trade-off is higher memory usage per request, but the speed gain outweighs it for real-time power work. DeepSeek-R1-671B stays on the 8xA100 node for heavy lifting where latency matters less.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B’s MoE claim ignores sharding overhead—EXCAVA’s 8xA100 node can’t hide it, so latency spikes will eat the "30-40% gain." DeepSeek-R1-671B’s dense architecture caps us at 6x the tokens/sec of a sharded MoE, but its stability and proven real-time performance make it the safer bet—run a 48-hour burn-in test on both to settle it.
